name: Dancing Dragons
description: Dancing Dragons is a Chinese-domino connecting game in which players extend a shared layout by matching legal ends while trying to empty their hands before opponents.

overview.description: Dancing Dragons is a Chinese-domino connecting game in which players extend a shared layout by matching legal ends while trying to empty their hands before opponents.

history.origins: Dancing Dragons is documented as a modern Chinese-domino line game format rather than a long-established classical gambling family.
timeline: Modern era: Documented in online domino indexes and reference pages.
Current: Played as a Chinese-domino connecting/shedding variant.
history.cultural: It is mostly encountered through rules compendia and enthusiast communities.
history.evolution: The game is treated as a contemporary indexed ruleset in the broader connecting domino genre.

setup.deck: One Chinese domino set of 32 tiles.
setup.dealing: Deal tiles evenly to players according to table convention; remaining tiles can be boneyard if used by local rules.
setup.equipment: Chinese domino tiles and table space for a line layout.

rules.objective: Be first to empty your hand, or finish with the lowest remaining pip burden if play blocks.
rules.gameplay: A starting tile opens the layout. On turn, a player places one legal matching tile to an open end. If no legal play exists, the player follows the table's draw-or-pass rule. The deal ends when a player goes out or all players are blocked.
keyRules: Play one legal matching tile to an open end each turn.
If blocked, follow draw-or-pass procedure defined by table rules.
Deal ends on first empty hand or complete block.

strategy.basic: Keep flexible tiles so you can answer multiple end states.
strategy.intermediate: Track exposed high-impact tiles to predict likely dead ends.
strategy.advanced: Shape end values to force opponents into low-probability responses.
tips: Avoid exposing a line end that only you can currently satisfy unless it also advances your exit.
Preserve at least one flexible response tile for late hand.

synthesis.shortDescription: Dancing Dragons is a Chinese-domino connecting game in Pagat's line index, focused on matching play and hand shedding.
